comment.narrative: DSROI Global 2022 was held in October-November, for a duration of six weeks. There were 72 participants, which most commonly describes themselves as: leaders, artists, activists and advocates. Their field of work includes GBV, gender equality, women’s rights and disability rights. 43 out of 72 participants identify themselves as persons with disabilities. The Institute is designed and taught by an international group of academics and activists in the disability rights field, specializing in sexual and reproductive rights from a Global South perspective.
2 - internatational conferences/alliance meetings attended by partners

GDS- WGG partners co-hosted a side event at the Summit–‘Dismantling ableism in sexual and reproductive health and rights: What kinds of cross-movement cooperation and transformational leadership do we need?’. As a participatory reflection circle, it brought together 50 activists from the Global South and Global North and the feminist, SRHR, and disability justice movements to explore how cross-movement cooperation collective advocacy strategies to dismantle ableism and promote reproductive justice. Discussions covered the invisibility of certain disability groups in SRHR frameworks, the persistence of ableist and gender-based violence, and the urgent need to advance disability-inclusive policies. The circle emphasised solidarity-building across movements and the importance of shared leadership and lived experience in driving systemic change. WGG also sponsored five delegates to attend GDS 2025, including women with disabilities leaders. They represent organisations such as the Kenyan Network of Women with Disabilities, Women with Disabilities Development Foundation Bangladesh, Women Spaces Africa, alongside CREA and IWRAW AP representatives. They engaged in advocacy and amplified the voices of their communities on global platforms. WGG helped the booth takeover of Women Enabled International to reach new audience and engage in important conversations with GDS attendees. Reconference- To mark its 25th year, CREA hosted its second Reconference in Kathmandu in a three-day global convening of feminist thinkers, activists, and practitioners. It was a space for collective reflection and strategic engagement by diverse feminist movements to reassess organising practices, leadership, and solidarity in response to contemporary challenges. Participatory with multi-modal formats, it included plenaries, teach-ins, workshops, strategy circles, lightning talks, book launches, performances, and film screenings. This supported inclusive engagement and dialogues across differences in identity, location, and movement roles. The participation of WGG partners from India, Bangladesh, and East Africa was both intentional and politically significant. Partners representing disability justice played a leading role in organising a Strategic Circle focused on developing actionable steps to counter ableism across movements. Partners from East Africa brought grounded community-organising experience to the dialogue, ensuring that East African movements were actively shaping global feminist strategy rather than remaining on the periphery.By engaging in diverse sessions, particularly those focused on movement sustainability and collective resilience, partners were able to reflect on burnout and the importance of feminist care. The Reconference served as a vital space for WGG partners to bridge the gap between localised struggles and global feminist organising, strengthening a shared vision for an inclusive and rights-based future.

GSWF (number of participants from outside of WGG partners, 15), AWID (number of participants who attend the WGG side event 20)The Global South Women’s Forum for Sustainable Development (GSWF) ias a forum is an overarching political response to the climate of civic participation in the sustainable development agenda which has hsiotrically lacked a feminist perspective rooted in Global South realities as well as as well as a dearth of feminist spaces for collective thinking and action on common struggles. In 2024, WGG will be leading the GSWF and inviting external actors from a cross section of movements across SA and EA to attend and engage with us. Those actors and movements which are outside of WGG currently will be enriched through the engagem,ent as will the WGG partners and collective. Addiitonally in 2024 December, WGG will be delivering a side event at the AWID conference focused on: Practising disability justice in GBV responses. What feminists need to understand and do better? We will be looking to strengthen movements and alliances throug the participants who attend that event.

GSWF - IWRAW AP led the Global South Women’s Forum on the theme of disability justice in October 2024, with over 70 participants from various movements. The forum focused on three specific topics: Leadership and Political Participation, Disability in the Context of a Changing World and Building our Political Agenda and Collective Ways of Work. As part of GSWF follow up, IWRAW AP initiated a workplan with young feminist leaders in 2025 to focus on integrating the accessibility agenda across various thematic areas associated with SGBV. AWID- The WGG Consortium organized a Session on Practicing Disability Justice in GBV responses: What feminists need to understand and do better, during AWID 2024 in Bangkok, Thailand. Despite the high risk of GBV, Women, Girls and Gender Diverse Persons with Disabilities (WGGDPWDs) often remain underrepresented in feminist responses to GBV. The session in AWID was aimed at shedding light on key issues, responses and collaborative aspirations at the intersection of GBV and Disability using a Disability Justice lens. The consortium created our sharing circles in a way that each circle had some WGG disability rights members as facilitators and then everyone else who came in brought their own understanding but the facilitators could steer the conversations skillfully so that the overall learnings were interesting and engaging for all. The session was held to a packed house, on the first day of the conference and saw over a 100 participants from diverse backgrounds taking part in the conversations.
There is a target of 1 unit for this period.

We took part in the International Conference of the Disability, Equity, Justice Working Group Civil 20 India. The international Conference was organised by Rising Flame in collaboration with Mariwala Health Initiative, Keshav Suri Foundation, and CREA. The conference had over 300 in-person participants from across 10 countries including India, and 1000 people joining in online throughout the day. Our participants were from diverse disabilities and chronic illnesses and nondisabled allies, from across geographical(urban and rural) and gender diversities. We are proud to share that we had civil society, government, multilaterals all together commit to disability inclusion and encouraging leadership of persons with disabilities through Nothing About Us Without Us.
